questions.q: Benzil, C₆H₅COCOC₆H₅, is heated with concentrated KOH and the mixture is then acidified. The product is:
questions.explain: OH⁻ adds to one carbonyl and a phenyl shifts to the neighbouring carbonyl carbon, so both phenyls end up on the carbon carrying OH, next to COOH. The product keeps all 14 carbons of benzil.

questions.q: Phenylglyoxal, C₆H₅COCHO, is treated with OH⁻ and then H₃O⁺. The product and the name of this variant are:
options: Benzoylformic acid, C₆H₅COCOOH; an aldol reaction
Benzoic acid and HCOOH; a haloform-type cleavage
Mandelic acid, C₆H₅CH(OH)COOH; an intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction
questions.explain: Here hydride, not phenyl, is the group that migrates, so the same pathway is called an intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction and gives mandelic acid.

questions.q: The rate-determining step of the benzilic acid rearrangement is:
options: The 1,2-migration of the aryl group to the neighbouring carbonyl carbon
Addition of hydroxide to a carbonyl carbon
Proton transfer from COOH to the alkoxide
Protonation of the carboxylate by H₃O⁺
questions.explain: Hydroxide addition is a fast, reversible equilibrium; the aryl shift that follows is slow. The rate is first order in diketone and first order in hydroxide.

questions.q: Phenanthrene-9,10-quinone is treated with OH⁻ and then acidified. The product is:
questions.explain: In a cyclic 1,2-diketone the migrating group is a ring bond, so the central six-membered ring contracts to a five-membered ring carrying both OH and COOH on one carbon (C₁₄H₈O₂ to C₁₄H₁₀O₃).
